Still, using Pre-War Formalwear now to reanimate Solitude (which has 3 or less mana value? No, Solitude is 5 MV) — actually Pre-War Formalwear returns a creature with MV 3 or less. The graveyard has Solitude (MV 5) and Windswept Heath (land). There's no valid creature with MV 3 or less in the graveyard to target with Pre-War Formalwear's ETB trigger, making the equipment somewhat wasted right now.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Stoneforge Mystic to put Pre-War Formalwear onto the battlefield from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Wait to use Stoneforge Mystic until there is a valid creature with MV 3 or less in the graveyard to reanimate with Pre-War Formalwear's ETB. Instead, tick up Aether Vial and hold mana open, potentially using Aether Vial to flash in Skyclave Apparition if needed.

annotations.description: Failed to crack Scalding Tarn at the beginning of their own turn. With 5 cards in graveyard, cracking Tarn would put them at 6 (one away from Threshold for Cabal Ritual's bonus mode). More importantly, cracking Tarn into a second black source would enable the line: tap both lands for BB, cast Cabal Ritual (BBB), cast Doomsday. Even if Doomsday this turn isn't optimal without an immediate draw effect post-Doomsday, not cracking the fetch delays the combo and gives the opponent more time to develop with Stoneforge Mystic and Aether Vial.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Scalding Tarn or taking any action at the beginning of their turn.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Scalding Tarn to fetch a Swamp or Island, advancing toward Threshold and potentially enabling Cabal Ritual into Doomsday this turn.

annotations.description: Aether Vial currently has 2 charge counters (placed turn 1 and turn 2 upkeeps). The player has Skyclave Apparition in hand, which costs exactly {1}{W}{W} (mana value 3, not 2). However, there are no opponent creatures on the battlefield to target with Skyclave Apparition's ETB, so vialing it in now would be suboptimal anyway. The real issue is declining a free Aether Vial activation when it could put a creature into play. With 2 counters, there may not be a matching creature in hand (Skyclave is MV 3, Overlord is MV 5, Solitude is MV 5). Actually, checking the hand: Pre-War Formalwear (MV 3, not a creature), Swords to Plowshares (MV 1), Overlord of the Balemurk (MV 5), Skyclave Apparition (MV 3). None of these are MV 2 creatures, so declining the Vial activation is correct since there's nothing to put in. The decision to pass is reasonable.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Aether Vial or cast Swords to Plowshares, passing without action.
annotations.betterLine: Passing is actually correct here - no MV 2 creatures in hand for Vial, and no creatures on opponent's board to Swords.

annotations.description: Libby had 2 untapped Underground Seas (2 mana available) and could have cast Cabal Ritual ({1}{B}) to generate {B}{B}{B}, then cast Doomsday ({B}{B}{B}) this turn to set up a winning pile. Instead, Libby incorrectly believed only 1 mana was available and passed, giving the opponent another turn to develop with Stoneforge Mystic and Aether Vial.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything, believing only 1 untapped land was available.
annotations.betterLine: Tap both Underground Seas to cast Cabal Ritual, generating {B}{B}{B}, then cast Doomsday to assemble a winning 5-card pile at 8 life.

annotations.description: Casting Cabal Ritual before Doomsday uses a valuable post-Doomsday resource for only 1 net extra black mana. Keeping Cabal Ritual in hand after Doomsday would give more flexibility to execute the 5-card pile, as it could generate mana on a future turn when threshold is more likely met.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Cabal Ritual before Doomsday, leaving only {B} floating and Lotus Petal on board post-Doomsday
annotations.betterLine: Cast Doomsday directly using 2 Underground Seas + Lotus Petal sacrifice for {B}{B}{B}, keeping Cabal Ritual in hand for post-Doomsday pile execution

annotations.description: Doomsday is on the stack resolving, which is one of the most dangerous combo spells in Legacy. The opponent is setting up a 5-card pile to win the game (typically with Thassa's Oracle or similar). Aether Vial has 2 charge counters (it's turn 4, and was played turn 1, so likely has ~3 counters, but even at 2 counters Skyclave Apparition costs 3). However, the critical missed opportunity is activating Aether Vial in response to Doomsday. If Vial has 3 counters, Skyclave Apparition could be put into play at instant speed — but there's nothing to exile with it yet since Doomsday is a sorcery on the stack. More importantly, the player should be considering whether any response is meaningful here. The real issue is that passing without any response to Doomsday — the premier combo spell — is questionable, but the available responses (Swords with no creature target, Vial with unclear counter count) may genuinely not help. However, if Aether Vial has enough counters, vialing in Skyclave Apparition in response could be relevant to have a body ready, and doing it at end of opponent's turn after Doomsday resolves would threaten to exile whatever combo piece they play. Not activating Vial here wastes the opportunity to deploy a threat while the opponent is tapped out.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Aether Vial or casting anything in response to Doomsday on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Vial in response to Doomsday to put Skyclave Apparition onto the battlefield (if Vial has 3 counters). This deploys a threat while the opponent is tapped out post-Doomsday and positions Skyclave to exile whatever combo piece the opponent plays from their Doomsday pile. Even without an immediate exile target, having a 2/2 body applies pressure against an opponent who just lost half their life.

annotations.description: During Doomsday pile construction, Lion's Eye Diamond was exiled instead of being included in the 5-card pile. LED is one of the most critical combo pieces for Doomsday piles, providing the mana needed to cast win conditions after drawing through the pile. Without LED, the pile likely cannot generate enough mana to execute a winning line, especially with only 2 tapped lands and a Lotus Petal for mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Lotus Petal as the 5th pile card while allowing Lion's Eye Diamond to be exiled.
annotations.betterLine: Include Lion's Eye Diamond in the Doomsday pile instead of one of the other selected cards. LED enables cracking for mana in response to draw spells, which is the core engine of nearly every Doomsday pile.

annotations.description: In Doomsday pile construction, Street Wraith was placed at the bottom of the pile (chosen first = bottommost). Street Wraith is the free cycling draw engine (pay 2 life to draw) that enables drawing through the Doomsday pile. It should typically be near the top so it can be cycled immediately to access further pile cards. With only Edge of Autumn in hand as an alternative draw method (sacrificing a land), putting Street Wraith at the bottom makes the pile much harder to execute.
annotations.actionTaken: Placed Street Wraith as the first selection (bottommost position) in the Doomsday pile ordering.
annotations.betterLine: Street Wraith should likely be placed on top (selected last) or near the top of the pile so it can be cycled immediately to draw into the next piece of the combo, with the win condition cards arranged below it in executable order.

annotations.description: In a Doomsday pile where speed is critical (at 8 life vs a Stoneforge Mystic deck), putting Personal Tutor on top instead of Polluted Delta wastes a draw step. Polluted Delta on top allows playing it as a land drop, cracking it for a land, then cycling Edge of Autumn (sacrifice a land, draw a card) to draw deeper into the pile on the same turn, accelerating the kill by a full turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Personal Tutor on top of library (Polluted Delta second), requiring spending a draw step and mana on the tutor before progressing through the pile.
annotations.betterLine: Put Polluted Delta on top so next turn they can play it, crack it for a land, and cycle Edge of Autumn to draw deeper into the pile immediately, saving a crucial turn.

annotations.description: At the beginning of turn 4 upkeep, the player declined to act when they could have activated Aether Vial (currently at 2 counters from prior upkeeps, matching Stoneforge Mystic's MV) or activated Stoneforge Mystic to put Pre-War Formalwear onto the battlefield. The opponent is at 8 life after casting Doomsday (losing half their life), meaning they're on a tight Doomsday pile plan. Activating Stoneforge Mystic here to put Pre-War Formalwear into play (returning Solitude from graveyard) would create significant pressure and a removal effect, potentially disrupting whatever the opponent is trying to do with their Doomsday pile. Passing with no action wastes tempo in a critical window where the opponent is vulnerable at 8 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities at the beginning of turn 4.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Stoneforge Mystic to put Pre-War Formalwear onto the battlefield, targeting Solitude in the graveyard. This creates a 5/4 vigilance lifelink creature whose ETB can exile an opponent's creature if needed, while applying significant clock pressure against the 8-life Doomsday opponent.

annotations.description: Cast Pre-War Formalwear for 3 mana with no valid creature target (MV 3 or less) in the graveyard - Solitude is MV 5 and Windswept Heath is a land. The ETB reanimation trigger is wasted. Against a post-Doomsday opponent at 8 life, maximizing pressure and holding interaction is critical. Additionally, even if they wanted the equipment, Stoneforge Mystic's activated ability could put it into play for only {1}{W} instead of hardcasting for {2}{W}.
annotations.actionTaken: Hardcast Pre-War Formalwear for 3 mana with no valid reanimation target in graveyard
annotations.betterLine: Cast Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd for {1}{W} to apply pressure against the 8-life opponent, hold up Swords to Plowshares with remaining mana as interaction against whatever the Doomsday pile produces. Could use Stoneforge's ability on a later turn to deploy the Formalwear if needed.

annotations.description: After resolving Doomsday, the library is a precisely ordered 5-card pile. Casting Personal Tutor shuffles the library (cards 2-5 get randomized), destroying the carefully arranged Doomsday pile order. This likely ruins the entire combo line that Doomsday was setting up, wasting the 3 mana and half their life spent on Doomsday.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Personal Tutor, which searches and shuffles the library, disrupting the Doomsday pile order.
annotations.betterLine: Cycle Edge of Autumn by sacrificing an Underground Sea to draw the top card of the Doomsday pile, progressing through the combo without disrupting pile order.

annotations.description: After resolving Doomsday, the library is a precisely ordered 5-card pile. Personal Tutor searches and SHUFFLES the library before putting the found card on top, which randomizes the remaining Doomsday pile cards and likely destroys the deterministic win sequence.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Personal Tutor, which shuffles the Doomsday pile
annotations.betterLine: Cycle Edge of Autumn by sacrificing an Underground Sea to draw the top card of the Doomsday pile without disrupting the pile order, which is the standard way to cantrip into a Doomsday pile

annotations.description: Opponent is at 6 life with no creatures to block. Attacking with only Stoneforge Mystic deals 1 damage instead of attacking with all creatures (Stoneforge Mystic 1/2, Phelia 2/2+, Skyclave Apparition 2/2) for at least 5 damage total, potentially lethal if Phelia has any +1/+1 counters or Pre-War Formalwear is equipped. Against a post-Doomsday opponent who is assembling a combo kill, failing to apply maximum pressure is game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Stoneforge Mystic (1 damage)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Stoneforge Mystic, Phelia, Skyclave Apparition) for at least 5 damage, putting opponent to 1 life or killing them outright if Phelia has counters.

annotations.description: Activated Aether Vial with no creature of the appropriate mana value in hand. The only creature in hand is Overlord of the Balemurk (MV 5), while Vial likely has 3 counters. The reasoning incorrectly states Skyclave Apparition is being put onto the battlefield, but it's already in play. This wastes the Vial tap for the turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Aether Vial at the beginning of turn with no valid creature in hand to put onto the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Do not activate Aether Vial since there are no creatures in hand matching its counter count. Proceed to combat with the existing board to attack for lethal (Phelia + Skyclave Apparition + Stoneforge Mystic likely deal 5+ damage against an opponent at 5 life).

annotations.description: Opponent is at 5 life. Timmy has Stoneforge Mystic (1/2), Skyclave Apparition (2/2), and Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd (2/2, likely with +1/+1 counters from flickering) on board with no opposing blockers. Instead of going to combat for the kill, Timmy is trying to cast an expensive creature pre-combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for {3}{B}{B} in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Go to combat and attack with Phelia, Skyclave Apparition, and Stoneforge Mystic for lethal damage (at least 5 power vs opponent at 5 life)
